about.credits_body: Based on the work of UxPlay (GPL-3.0), doubletake (LGPL-3.0), MultiDrop, playfair and FFmpeg's AAC decoder (LGPL-2.1). See the NOTICE file for details.
about.license_body: RustPlay is free software: you can redistribute it and modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (GPL-3.0-or-later). It comes with no warranty.
about.subtitle: About RustPlay.
about.support_body: RustPlay is free and open source. If you find it useful, you can browse the code, contribute or buy me a coffee.
about.tagline: Send your PC's screen to a TV and receive your iPhone's, with hardware-accelerated video.
about.trademarks_body: AirPlay, Apple TV, iPhone, iPad and Mac are trademarks of Apple Inc. RustPlay is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple.
about.why_body: I got tired of seeing apps on the Microsoft Store charge a subscription for something as simple as showing your iPhone screen on your PC. RustPlay exists to prove that nobody needs to be squeezed: it's free, open and ad-free.
about.why_quote: “I can hear the drums of liberation...”

setup.audio.none: There is no active audio output, so you won't hear the sound from your iPhone. Connect speakers or headphones.
setup.audio.title: Audio
setup.firewall.blocked: A firewall rule blocks RustPlay on private networks. Remove or disable that rule in the firewall's advanced settings.
setup.firewall.missing: There is no rule that allows RustPlay on private networks. Windows will ask the first time, or you can allow it now (it needs administrator permission).
setup.firewall.off: Windows Firewall is off for private networks, so nothing blocks RustPlay.
setup.firewall.ok: Windows Firewall allows RustPlay on private networks.
setup.firewall.partial: The firewall allows RustPlay only partially: {detail} is missing. Allow it for everything (it needs administrator permission).
setup.firewall.title: Windows Firewall
setup.gpu.no_decoder: No H.264 decoder is available, so receiving the screen won't work ({detail}).
setup.gpu.no_device: No graphics device with video support could be created ({detail}). Update your graphics driver.
setup.gpu.no_encoder: No H.264 encoder is available, so sending your screen won't work ({detail}).
setup.gpu.ok: Your graphics card can decode and encode H.264 video in hardware.
setup.gpu.software_both: Video is decoded and encoded by the processor. It works, but it uses more CPU. Updating the graphics driver may help.
setup.gpu.software_decoder: Received video is decoded by the processor. It works, but it uses more CPU.
setup.gpu.software_encoder: Video you send is encoded by the processor. It works, but it uses more CPU and may add delay.
setup.gpu.title: Graphics and video
setup.mdns.failed: RustPlay couldn't announce itself on the network, so the iPhone won't see it ({detail}). Check that the DNS Client service is running.
setup.mdns.ok: RustPlay can announce itself on the network, so your iPhone sees it in the AirPlay list.
setup.mdns.shared: RustPlay can announce itself, but another discovery service is running: {detail}. It usually works, but if your iPhone doesn't see RustPlay, close that program or restart it.
setup.mdns.title: Discovery (Bonjour)
setup.network.none: You aren't connected to any network. Connect to the same Wi-Fi or cable network as your Apple devices.
setup.network.ok: Your network is private ({detail}), so your iPhone can find RustPlay.
setup.network.public: “{detail}” is a public network. Windows blocks incoming AirPlay connections there. Switch it to Private in the network settings.
setup.network.title: Network profile
setup.port.busy: Port {detail} is used by another program, so the receiver can't start. Close it or restart the PC.
setup.port.free: Port {detail} is free for the receiver.
setup.port.ours: Port {detail} is in use by RustPlay's own receiver.
setup.port.title: Receiver port
setup.subtitle: These checks tell you whether your PC is ready to send and receive with AirPlay. Nothing is changed unless you press a button.
setup.title: System check
update.err.download: The download failed. Try again, or open the release page.
update.err.mismatch: The downloaded file doesn't match its checksum and was deleted. Try again later.
update.err.no_checksum: This release has no checksum file, so RustPlay won't run its installer. Download it from the release page.
update.manual_portable: The portable version is updated by hand from the release page
update.notify_body: Get it from the project page on GitHub.
update.ready: The update is downloaded and verified
update.ready_desc: Its checksum matches the one published with the release.

welcome.feature.apps.title: Videos, photos and music
welcome.feature.receive.body: Mirror the screen and sound of your iPhone or iPad in a window on the computer.
welcome.feature.receive.title: See your iPhone on the PC

welcome.feature.send.title: Send your PC to the TV

welcome.features.title: What you can do
welcome.receive.s1_body: On the Receive page, switch it on. Your PC will appear on the network as “{name}”.
welcome.receive.s2_body: Swipe down from the top-right corner of the iPhone and tap “Screen Mirroring”.
welcome.receive.s3_body: Your screen appears in a window. To finish, close the window or use “Stop sharing”.
welcome.receive.subtitle: It is the easiest way: nothing to install on the phone.
welcome.receive.title: Receive from your iPhone
welcome.send.s1_body: RustPlay looks for devices on your network and lists them.
welcome.send.s2_body: Press “Mirror”. If the TV shows a code, type it the first time.
welcome.send.s3_body: In the options you can send the whole screen or just one window, and star your TV.
welcome.send.subtitle: Works with Apple TV and many TVs with built-in AirPlay.
welcome.send.title: Send to a TV
welcome.subtitle: Receive your iPhone’s screen on the PC or send the PC’s screen to a TV, with GPU-accelerated video. Free, open source and ad-free.
